claims.text: Orbi Cloud recorded a median cost of $0.082 per merged delivery off-peak across 169 merged deliveries between 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-05, all on deepseek-flash.
In Orbi Cloud's 169-delivery sample, the 90th percentile cost per merged delivery was $0.22, the mean was $0.11, and all 169 deliveries together cost $18.45 (off-peak).

Orbi's earlier hand-measured sample of 20 merged PRs (22-24 September 2026, deepseek-flash) had a median cost of $0.125 off-peak and $0.249 at peak, a mean of $0.152 off-peak, a P90 of $0.298 off-peak, and a maximum of $0.417 off-peak.
The 20-PR Orbi sample had a median of 10,612,802 tokens per merged PR, a median runtime of 60.4 minutes, and a median of 156 model requests.

DeepSeek deepseek-flash off-peak prices used by Orbi: cache hit $0.003 per million tokens, cache miss $0.15 per million, output $0.60 per million; peak weekday hours (01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC) double every price.
In Orbi's 169-delivery sample, the median share of input tokens read from cache per delivery was 97.8%.

Across 46 Orbi deliveries (as of 2026-09-12, including unmerged work), the median was 2,220,637 totalTokens per delivery, p90 13,290,932, max 37,627,783, and mean 4,742,066; the token mix was 95.9% cache reads, 3.4% input, 0.7% output.
Orbi states that on an endpoint without prompt caching, where every token bills as a miss, the same work would cost roughly an order of magnitude more; a cache hit costs 1/50 of a miss.
Every Orbi delivery runs two agent sessions: an implementation, then an independent review that can repair the branch and rerun the suite.

In llm-track's worked example, a five-call PR review costs $0.475 without prompt caching and $0.274 with caching of 30,000 repeated tokens (written at $2.50 per million, read at $0.20 per million), about 42% less.

llm-track recommends labeling every call with the agent as the feature and the team or repo as the customer, then dividing spend by merged PRs; its worked example yields $0.274 per PR review, $1.03 per merged PR, and about $67 per engineer per month.

Busfactor's hypothetical worked example puts cost per merged PR from $4.52 at one team to $30.00 at another across the same 40 developers; the $30.00 team had $200 in seats but $1,300 in metered usage.
Busfactor cites Anthropic documentation that agent teams use approximately 7x more tokens than standard sessions when teammates run in plan mode.
LangChain reports that prompt caching cut token cost by 49-80% on real Deep Agents trajectories, including -77% for claude-haiku-4-5 using Anthropic's explicit breakpoints and -80% for gpt-5.4-mini.
LangChain cites research stating prompt caching can reduce inference token cost by 41-80%.

Google's token management policies use three resources: TokenAggregationPolicy (groups requests by project, AI application, agent identity, model, or custom headers/API keys), TokenBudgetPolicy (token pools), and CostPerTokenPolicy (overrides default per-model pricing used for estimated cost).

Each Google TokenBudgetPolicy token pool specifies a max token count, an hourly or daily reset window (daily resets at midnight Pacific Time), optional target models, an alert threshold, and an enforcement mode; strict enforcement returns HTTP 429 when the budget is exhausted.

Google's gateway checks the budget before the request but reconciles actual input, output, and cached token counts only after the response, so concurrent requests admitted before a pool reaches maxTokens can exceed the limit before later requests get 429.

Google's token management limits are one policy of each type per project scope, at most 10 aggregation rules and 10 token pools; requests to models outside a pool's target list are not blocked and are recorded with pool name 'undefined'.
Google states a single LLM HTTP request can consume from a dozen to over 100,000 tokens, so request-count rate limiting is insufficient and a runaway agent loop can exhaust shared quotas.

FinOps LLM's illustrative policy template sets max workflow cost $0.20, max attempt reservation $0.05, daily owner budget $50, max 6 model attempts, 4 tool attempts, 0 subagents, and a 120-second deadline, with an economy default model and a premium fallback requiring a new reservation.

FinOps LLM recommends atomically reserving each attempt against both the workflow and owner daily budgets before dispatch, retaining reservations for timed-out calls until usage is reconciled, and stopping before dispatch if a price is unknown.

In FinOps LLM's synthetic ledger a workflow costs $0.031 (assumed $2 input/$10 output per million tokens); with 100 attempted workflows and 90 passing, cost per successful task is $3.10/90, about $0.0344.

AWS Well-Architected agentic AI lens advises tracking cost-per-correct-response, token consumption, cache hit rate, and cascade escalation rate per model tier and feeding them back into routing and caching decisions.

AgenFleet budgets are set per agent via limits (e.g., dailyTokenBudget 300000, monthlyTokenBudget 6000000, alertThreshold 0.8); an alert fires at the threshold and the agent pauses for the rest of the day when the daily budget is exhausted.
